meta.scope: V1 LOCAL FR single-box; soketi WS :6001 frequently down in dev -> polling fallback

B3_kds_dual_parallel_poll.summary: When WS is down, KitchenDisplaySystemComponent runs TWO independent poll loops at once: (1) a coarse setInterval at _pollingInterval() (5000ms WS-down / 60000ms WS-up) that fetches the FULL uncached board via Vuex kitchenDisplaySystemOrder/lists -> GET admin/kds-order; (2) the adaptive delta loop via kdsSyncService (cached 5s server-side, GET /api/admin/kds-order/sync) whose 'sync' listener also triggers _debouncedRefresh() which re-fetches the SAME full board. Net: redundant full-board fetches plus a delta fetch every WS-down tick.

loop_1_coarse_board_poll.role: Full uncached board refetch (the redundant one)
loop_1_coarse_board_poll.restart_on_ws_change: KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:1909-1912 _restartPolling() = stopAutoRefresh()+startAutoRefresh(); bound to ws connected/disconnected at :1880-1889 (_bindWsService)
loop_1_coarse_board_poll.vuex_action: resources/js/store/modules/kitchenDisplaySystemOrder.js:21-36 lists() -> axios.get('admin/kds-order' + requestHandler(payload)) ; NO since-param, NO client cache, full board
loop_1_coarse_board_poll.cadence_note: Hardcoded per-surface (NOT config-read) by deliberate HEAL B.3 2026-05-19 anchor at :1901-1907. 5s WS-down protects ~5s kitchen-staleness budget.

loop_2_delta_sync_poll.role: Adaptive delta sync (cached, the one that should be sole fallback)
loop_2_delta_sync_poll.cadence_formula: KdsSyncService.js:297-320 _baseCadence(): WS CONNECTED => Infinity (drift-only 60s timer at :353-362); WS RECONNECTING/DEGRADED => degradedBaseMs 5000 + jitter 2000 (or highActivity 3000+1000); WS DISCONNECTED/SESSION_INVALID => disconnectedBaseMs 10000 + jitter 3000 (or highActivity 3000+1000)
loop_2_delta_sync_poll.clamps: KdsSyncService.js:25-27 CADENCE_FLOOR_MS 250 / CADENCE_CEILING_MS 60000 / JITTER_CEILING_MS 30000 (anti-misconfig DoS, Wave 3/3b)
loop_2_delta_sync_poll.delta_query: app/Services/KdsSyncService.php:98-119 active statuses [ACCEPT,PREPARING,PREPARED], where updated_at >= since, today-window (sargable whereBetween, TZ-aware Paris-local :91-94), limit 50, eager-loads orderItems.orderItem/address/user/diningTable (:96-98)
loop_2_delta_sync_poll.leaves_window: app/Services/KdsSyncService.php:136-155 deleted_ids = softDeleted(deleted_at>=since) merged with left-window (status in DELIVERED/CANCELED/REJECTED)
loop_2_delta_sync_poll.what_happens_on_delta: KdsSyncService.js:204 _emit('sync', payload) -> KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:1544-1553 listener: if hasFreshOrders||hasDeletes -> this._debouncedRefresh()

the_redundancy_crux.debounced_refresh: KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:2443-2451 _debouncedRefresh() => 300ms setTimeout -> _refreshWithCurrentFilter() + items() (i.e. the SAME full uncached board fetch as loop 1)
the_redundancy_crux.double_count_when_ws_down: Every WS-down tick: (a) loop-1 setInterval at 5s fires refreshOrderList() = full board; (b) loop-2 delta poll (5-10s) returns deltas; if any fresh/deleted, its 'sync' listener fires _debouncedRefresh() = ANOTHER full board fetch. So the cheap delta is consumed only to TRIGGER a full uncached board fetch, while loop-1 already does the full fetch on its own clock. The delta's bandwidth/cache win is largely thrown away.
the_redundancy_crux.confirmed_parallel: Both started unconditionally in the same mounted() hook: startAutoRefresh() at :1492 AND kdsSyncService.start() at :1558. Neither gates on the other.
the_redundancy_crux.oss_is_NOT_dual: OrderStatusScreenComponent.vue mounted() (:45-47) only closeSidebar() - NO board poll on the OSS surface. The OSS poll is the SINGLE OssSyncService loop (resources/js/services/OssSyncService.js) which dispatches orderStatusScreenOrder/lists. So the dual-parallel defect is KDS-only; OSS is the reference single-loop pattern.

oss_sync_reference_for_design.cadence: OssSyncService.js:8-27 intervalMsWhenConnected 60000 / intervalMsWhenDisconnected 2000; backoff 5000->30000; visibility burst-poll (:208-252); throwing-listener guard (:448-467 #7)
oss_sync_reference_for_design.why_2s_disconnected: OssSyncService.js:10-16 tightened 5000->2000 to meet SYNC-2 8s budget (POS pay -> OSS visible) on polling-only fallback; clamp [250,60000] (:34-35,:437-442)
oss_sync_reference_for_design.lesson: OSS proves a single adaptive loop CAN meet the staleness budget on WS-down. KDS can converge to the same shape.

option_A_preferred.title: Make the delta loop the SOLE WS-down fallback; suspend the coarse board setInterval while delta is the live driver
option_A_preferred.change: In _pollingInterval()/startAutoRefresh(): when WS is down, do NOT arm the 5s full-board setInterval (or set it to a slow safety-net e.g. 60s drift-poll mirroring KdsSyncService _schedule Infinity-branch). Keep loop-1 only as a coarse drift/safety re-sync, let kdsSyncService deltas drive _debouncedRefresh as today. Keeps server cache benefit, removes the every-5s full uncached board fetch.
option_A_preferred.risk: Must guarantee delta loop ALWAYS runs on this surface (it does: started unconditionally :1558) and that a first-load full board still happens (it does: mounted() refreshOrderList() :1491). Edge: if kdsSyncService errors silently the board could stale -> keep a slow (60s) safety setInterval as drift backstop, NOT the 5s one.

option_B_alternative.title: Cache list() server-side (mirror KdsSyncService.php Cache::remember on the admin/kds-order full-board endpoint)
option_B_alternative.change: Add a short (e.g. 2-5s) Cache::remember to the KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService::list path so the 5s coarse poll and the _debouncedRefresh full fetch coalesce instead of hitting the DB twice. Less elegant: keeps both loops but de-duplicates DB cost.
option_B_alternative.risk: list() returns filter-dependent payload (props.search) -> cache key must salt branch_id + status filter + today-window bucket; staleness must stay <= 5s budget. Touches a backend service in the KDS read path.

minimal_safe_fix_options.recommendation: Option A (suspend/slow the redundant coarse loop, delta becomes the sole active WS-down fallback with a 60s drift safety-net). Smaller blast radius, no new backend cache key, mirrors the OSS single-loop shape and KdsSyncService's own Infinity/drift pattern.

why_gated_sync_contract_invariant.shared_zone: CLAUDE.md section 6 / SYNC_CONTRACT.md: KDS<->OSS<->customer-tracker realtime sync is a SHARED zone (LOCK+gate). Polling cadence is the WS-down degradation path of that contract.
why_gated_sync_contract_invariant.invariant_at_risk: Kitchen-staleness budget: orders MUST surface on the KDS board within ~5s of payment when WS is down (anchor comment KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:1901-1907). If Option A wrongly removed BOTH the 5s board poll AND failed to guarantee delta-driven refresh, the kitchen would go blind during a WS outage -> orders never cook -> customer waits -> NF525-adjacent operational failure. Symmetric risk: OSS customer wall (SYNC-2 8s budget, OssSyncService.js:11-16) and the tracker depend on the same payment->display chain.
why_gated_sync_contract_invariant.cross_surface: A naive change to KdsSyncService.php delta query (e.g. window/limit/eager-load) would ALSO affect any other consumer of /api/admin/kds-order/sync and the OSS budget that assumes the kitchen progresses. Hence: change the CLIENT loop arming (Option A) NOT the shared delta contract, and gate the LOCK on SYNC_CONTRACT.
why_gated_sync_contract_invariant.verdict: OWNER GATE required because it modifies the WS-down degradation behavior of a SYNC-CONTRACT shared zone, even though no NF525/frozen file is touched.

bundles.summary: The 7MB+ figures are DEV (unminified, mode=development via `mix` / `npm run development`). A production build (`mix --production` / `npm run production`) minifies + tree-shakes and would cut these dramatically. vendor.js IS extracted and IS loaded by the blades before app/pos-app, but pos-app.js still appears to inline the Vue runtime (vendor not fully deduped from the second entry).

build_mode_reality.current_build_is_dev: package.json scripts: 'development':'mix' (default 'dev'), 'production':'mix --production'. The on-disk bundles are the dev build.
build_mode_reality.note: gzip of the DEV bundle already ~1.1MB for app.js; a --production build minifies first (drops comments/whitespace/dead code, Vue feature-flag DCE already wired at webpack.mix.js:11-19) THEN gzips, so realistic prod-gzip is materially smaller again. The 7MB raw number is not the shipped weight even today (gzip on the wire), and is a dev artifact.

chunk_architecture.extract_list: webpack.mix.js:59-79 — vue, vuex, vue-router, axios, vue-toastification, vue3-simple-alert, vue-next-select, vue3-apexcharts, apexcharts, vue-i18n, vuex-persistedstate, laravel-echo, pusher-js, dompurify, vue-element-loading, swiper -> emitted as vendor.js + manifest.js
chunk_architecture.admin_shell_kds_oss_kiosk_are_dynamic_ch: admin-shell.js / admin-kds.js / admin-oss.js / admin-reports.js / kiosk-*.js are lazy webpack chunks produced by dynamic import() with webpackChunkName, e.g. resources/js/router/modules/administratorRoutes.js:5-8 import(/* webpackChunkName: "admin-shell" */ ...). They are code-split OUT of app.js and loaded on-route. They are NOT separate mix.js() calls -> a single `mix --production` minifies all of them.
chunk_architecture.vendor_not_fully_shared_into_pos_app: grep: public/js/pos-app.js contains 4 'Vue warn' string hits + 2 webpackChunk markers; vendor.js contains 0 'Vue warn'. Comment webpack.mix.js:48-54 acknowledges Mix applies extract() GLOBALLY so it SHOULD govern pos-app.js too, but the dev bundle shows Vue inlined in pos-app.js. This matches the prompt's 'vendor.js not shared into entries' observation for the POS entry — worth confirming post-`--production` whether pos-app dedups against vendor.js (CI guard tools/lint/pos_app_size.mjs referenced at webpack.mix.js:53 asserts a gz ceiling).

frozen_pos_wizard_wiring.pos_wizard_is_NOT_a_mix_entry: CONFIRMED: `grep pos-wizard public/mix-manifest.json` => 0 hits. pos-wizard.js (296912 bytes) is hand-written Vanilla JS, NOT compiled by Mix.
frozen_pos_wizard_wiring.loaded_via_asset_not_mix: resources/views/admin-pos-v4.blade.php:136 <script src="{{ asset('js/pos-wizard.js') }}?v=9-{{ time() }}"> ; CSS at :35 asset('css/pos-wizard.css'). Also master.blade.php:272 / :47.
frozen_pos_wizard_wiring.implication: A `mix --production` run does NOT touch, re-minify, re-hash, or re-wire pos-wizard.js or pos-wizard.css — they are served raw via asset() with a time()-based cache-bust, completely outside the Mix pipeline. FROZEN zone (CLAUDE.md section 7) is therefore NOT affected by a production build of the Mix entries.
frozen_pos_wizard_wiring.blade_load_order_critical: admin-pos-v4.blade.php:118-120 manifest.js -> vendor.js -> pos-app.js (all via mix()); pos-wizard.js loaded later at :136 via asset(). master.blade.php:255-257 manifest->vendor->app.js. The mix() helper resolves the hashed filename from mix-manifest.json, so .version() content-hashes are honored as long as the build regenerates mix-manifest.json.

Adding/extending the vendor extract([]) list at webpack.mix.js:59-79 with libs already imported (pure caching optimization; emits to vendor.js which blades already load).
Verifying/raising the CI gz ceiling guard tools/lint/pos_app_size.mjs.
GATED_or_caution: Adding `.extract()` to the pos-app.js chain (webpack.mix.js:55) to force vendor dedup from the POS entry: comment :48-54 warns Mix extract() is GLOBAL and per-entry extract semantics are version-fragile; a regression here changes what the FROZEN-wiring POS surface (admin-pos-v4.blade.php) loads -> verify blade load order (manifest->vendor->pos-app) still holds and pos-wizard.js shim still initializes against the (now possibly reordered) globals. Treat as caution + visual/Playwright proof on /admin/pos-v4, not silent.

Any change to blade asset ordering on admin-pos-v4.blade.php or master.blade.php -> those blades are in/adjacent to the FROZEN POS-wizard wiring (CLAUDE.md section 7 lists admin-pos-v4.blade.php as frozen) -> OWNER GATE.
webpack_mix_change_safe_vs_gated.key_clarification: admin-pos-v4.blade.php IS listed FROZEN in CLAUDE.md section 7. So editing the blade = gated. But running `mix --production` and editing webpack.mix.js (non-frozen) to improve extraction does NOT require editing that blade, because mix() already reads hashed names from mix-manifest.json. The production build is therefore largely SAFE; only a blade edit or a pos-app extract() change crosses into gated territory.
